questions.question: Startup India was launched under the ___________.

options.text: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Commerce and Industry.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Startup India is a flagship initiative launched by the Government of India** in **2016 **to build a **strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups in the country.**
 
• The initiative is driven by the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry.**
 
• It aims to** drive sustainable economic growth and generate large-scale employment opportunities.**
 
• The initiative involves several measures** including simplification and handholding, funding support and incentives, and an industry-academia partnership and incubation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The Startup India initiative plans to empower startups through a** 19-point action plan.**
 
• This plan includes areas such as simplification and handholding, funding support and incentives, and industry-academia partnerships and incubation.
 
• An additional area of focus is to discard restrictive **States Government policies within this domain, such as License Raj, Land Permissions, Foreign Investment Proposals, and Environmental Clearances.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
 

 Ministry
 Minister
 Brief Description
 
 

 Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
 Dharmendra Pradhan
 This ministry is responsible for coordinating all skill development efforts across the country. It aims to remove the disconnect between demand and supply of skilled manpower, to build the new skills and innovative thinking not only for existing jobs but also for jobs that are to be created.
 
 

 Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
 Virendra Kumar
 This ministry is responsible for the welfare of people belonging to socially and economically backward classes, minorities, and other marginalized groups. It works to promote their education, employment, and social and economic development.
 
 

 Ministry of Labour and Employment
 Bhupender Yadav
 This ministry is responsible for the welfare of workers in India. It enforces labor laws, provides social security benefits, and promotes employment.
 
 

 Ministry of Commerce and Industry
 Piyush Goyal
 This ministry is responsible for the development of India's trade and industry. It promotes exports, attracts foreign investment, and regulates markets.

questions.question: It is used in making gunny bags, mats, ropes, yarn, carpets and other artefacts. Which crop is being spoken about here?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related with the primary sector of economy?
questions.solution:
The answer is __**Banking**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Banking is not a primary sector activity** because** it does not involve the extraction or production of raw materials.**
 
• Instead, banking is a **Tertiary sector activity because it involves the processing and distribution of goods and services that have been produced by the primary sector.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The primary sector is the foundation of the economy, as it provides the raw materials that are used to produce goods and services in the secondary and tertiary sectors.
 
• The primary sector is a major source of employment in many countries, particularly developing countries.
 
• The primary sector is facing a number of challenges, including climate change, population growth, and competition from foreign producers.
 
• The main keyword in the question is "related".
 
• Banking is not directly related to the extraction or production of raw materials, so it is not a primary sector activity.
 
• **Here are some other examples of primary sector activities:**
 
 
• Agriculture
 
• Fishing
 
• Forestry
 
• Mining
 
• Oil and gas extraction
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 Sector
 Description
 Examples
 
 

 Primary
 Extracts raw materials from nature
 Agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, quarrying
 
 

 Secondary
 Converts raw materials into finished goods
 Manufacturing, construction
 
 

 Tertiary
 Provides services to people and businesses
 Transportation, communication, retail, education, healthcare, tourism

questions.question: The intervention of the government whether to expand demand or reduce it constitutes the __________ function.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stabilization.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The government's intervention in the economy to expand or reduce demand is called a** stabilization policy.**
 
• **This is done to prevent the economy from going into recession or experiencing high inflation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal policy:**

 
 
• **​**The government can change its spending and tax levels to stimulate or slow down the economy.
 
• For example, during a recession, the government might increase spending on infrastructure projects or unemployment benefits.
 
• This would put more money into the economy and help to boost demand.
 
 
 
• **Monetary policy**
 
 
• ** **The government can change the interest rates that it charges banks to borrow money.
 
• This can affect the amount of money that banks lend to businesses and consumers, which can in turn affect the level of economic activity.
 
• For example, if the government wants to stimulate the economy, it might lower interest rates.
 
• This would make it cheaper for businesses to borrow money, which would encourage them to invest and hire more workers.
 
 
 
• **Stabilization: **The act of stabilizing something, such as the economy.
 
 
• Stabilization policy is a complex and controversial topic.
 
• Some economists believe that the government should play a more active role in managing the economy, while others believe that the market should be allowed to operate freely.
 
• Function: The purpose or role of something.

questions.question: Sattriya, is the classical dance form of which of the following states?

• It is characterized by its **graceful movements, intricate footwork, and use of traditional Assamese costumes and music.**

• Sankardeva was a **native of Assam, and he founded a number of monasteries in the region.**
 
• Sattriya was originally performed in these monasteries as a way to spread Sankardeva's teachings.
 
• Sattriya is a combination of f**olk dances, martial arts, and classical Indian dance forms.**
 
• This makes it a unique and distinctive dance form.
 
• Sattriya is characterized by its** graceful movements, intricate footwork, and use of traditional Assamese costumes and music.**
 
• These elements combine to create a beautiful and captivating dance form.
 
• Sattriya is a living tradition that is still performed today.
 
• **There are many schools and academies that teach Sattriya, and there are regular performances of Sattriya dance.**
 
• Sattriya has been recognized as one of the** eight classical dance forms of India.**

questions.question: In which region did the Swadeshi Movement have the strongest impact on people?
questions.solution:
the correct answer is __**Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swadeshi Movement had the strongest impact on the people of Bengal.**
 
• The movement was a **boycott of British goods and a promotion of Indian-made goods.**
 
• It was started in **1905 **in response to the British decision to partition Bengal.
 
• The movement was led by **Bengali intellectuals and students, and it quickly spread throughout the province.**

 
• The **Swadeshi Movement had a number of important impacts on the people of Bengal.**
 
• **First**, it helped to raise national consciousness and to create a sense of unity among Bengalis.
 
• **Second**, it helped to develop a sense of economic self-reliance among Bengalis.
 
• **Third**, it helped to create a new generation of political leaders who would later play a leading role in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Region
 
 

 Kashmir
 The Swadeshi Movement had a limited impact in Kashmir. This was due to a number of factors, including the region's remote location, its Muslim majority, and the strong influence of the Maharaja.
 
 

 Berar
 The Swadeshi Movement had a small impact in Berar. This was due to the region's small population and its distance from the centers of the movement.
 
 

 United Provinces
 The Swadeshi Movement had a moderate impact in the United Provinces. This was due to the region's large population and its proximity to the centers of the movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Swadeshi Movement__

 
 
• The movement had its roots in the anti-partition movement which was started to oppose Lord Curzon’s decision of dividing the province of Bengal.
 
• The Anti-Partition Campaign was launched by Moderates to exert pressure on the government to prevent the unjust partition of Bengal from being implemented.
 
• In the 1906 Congress Session held at Calcutta, the INC under the presidentship of Dadabhai Naoroji declared self-government or Swaraj as the goal of INC.
 
• The Extremists (or the Garam Dal) gained a dominant influence over the Swadeshi Movement in Bengal after 1905 till 1908.
 
• School and college students were the most active participants of the movement.
 
• Traditionally home-centered women too took active part in the movement.
 
• By 1908, the Swadeshi Movement was almost over in an open phase due to government’s violent repression.

questions.question: In a badminton singles game, if both the players are on 29 points then at what point will one of them win the game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30th point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In a game of badminton,** under the current rules set by the** Badminton World Federation, a singles match is won by the player who first scores 21 points, unless the score reaches 20-all.**
 
• When the score is tied at **20-all, the side which gains a two-point lead first wins that game.**
 
• However, if the score becomes **29-all, the side scoring the 30th point wins that game.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **About Badminton:**
 
• **Playing Area:**
 
 
• **​**Unlike doubles, the entire width of the court is not used in a singles match.
 
• The boundaries are defined by the outer lines of the length and the inner lines of the width.
 
 
 
• **Scoring:**
 
 
• **​**A match consists of the best of three games of 21 points each.
 
• Every time there's a serve, a point is scored.
 
• The side winning a rally adds a point to its score.
 
 
 
• **Service Rules:**
 
 
• **​**At the start of the game, the server serves from the right service court if their score is even, and from the left if their score is odd.
 
• After winning a point, the server switches service courts and continues serving.
 
 
 
• **Tied Score:**
 
 
• **​**In case the score reaches 20-all, the side which gains a two-point lead first, wins that game.
 
• However, if the score becomes 29-all, the side scoring the 30th point wins that game.
 
 
 
• **Strategy:**
 
 
• Singles badminton requires excellent control over the shuttlecock because the objective is to move the opponent around the court, making them run back and forth in order to create space.
 
• Stamina and agility are key, as the player has to cover the entire court by themselves.

questions.question: What is the white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulphate and barium chloride?
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Barium sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulfate and barium chloride is barium sulfate.
 
• The chemical reaction is as follows:

**Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)**

 
• In this reaction, the sodium and chloride ions from each reactant switch places to form sodium chloride and barium sulfate.
 
• Barium sulfate is a white, insoluble precipitate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Ravikirti composed prashasti of which of following Chalukya rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ravikirti was a Jain court poet and he composed the **Aihole Prashasti, which is also known as the Aihole Inscription.**
 
• The **Aihole Prashasti, written in Sanskrit, **provides a detailed account of the victories and achievements of** Pulakeshin II.**
 
• **Pulakeshin II was a significant Chalukya ruler** who is** known for successfully defending his kingdom against the north Indian Emperor Harsha, as mentioned in the Aihole Prashasti.**
 
• This historical document is a valuable source for the h**istory of the Deccan during the 6th century, as it provides a detailed account of the Chalukyan lineage and genealogy of its kings, up to Pulakeshin II.**
 
• **It is also an important document for the study of the development of Sanskrit literature.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Chalukya Ruler
 Reign
 Significant Achievements
 
 
 
 

 Mangalesha I
 597-610 CE
 He was the younger brother of Pulakeshin I and is known for his military campaigns, particularly against the Nalas and Mauryas of Konkana.
 
 

 Pulakeshin II
 610-642 CE
 He is the most notable ruler of the Chalukya dynasty. His court poet, Ravikirti, composed the Aihole Prashasti which provides detailed accounts of his victories and reign. He successfully defended his kingdom against Emperor Harsha.
 
 

 Kirtivarman II
 746-753 CE
 He was the last Badami Chalukya ruler. His reign ended with the defeat by the Rashtrakuta king Dantidurga, leading to the rise of the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
 

 Vikramaditya IV
 1076-1126 CE
 He was a Western Chalukya ruler, known for his wars against the Cholas and Hoysalas. Under his reign, the Western Chalukyas saw a cultural resurgence with prolific contributions in the fields of literature and architecture.

questions.question: Loo is a characteristic feature of which season?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Loo:

 
 
• Loo is a type of local wind that blows in some regions of India and Pakistan.
 
• Harmful Wind
 
• In the plains of northern India and Pakistan, sometimes a very hot and dry wind blows from the west in the months of May and June, usually in the afternoons.
 
• It is known as its temperature invariably ranges between 45°C and 50°C. It may cause sunstroke to people.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The movement of air from high-pressure to low-pressure areas is called wind.
 
• Winds are broadly classified into three types:
 
 
• Permanent Winds
 
• Seasonal Winds
 
• Local Winds
 
 
 
• Local Winds are winds that blow only during a particular period of the day or year in a small area.
 
• Some of the local winds with the area of flow are:
 
 
• Chinook- Rockies
 
• Foehn- Alps
 
• Loo- Gangetic plain, North India and Pakistan
 
• Sirocco- Sahara
 
• Mistral- Spain
 
• Blizzard- Polar regions of Canada and the USA

questions.question: How many balanced meals of average size each day should adolescents have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nutrition:**

 
 
• **​**Adolescents are in a** stage of rapid growth and development.**
 
• **They need balanced and nutritious meals to support this growth.**
 
• Three balanced meals a day can help provide the necessary **nutrients, vitamins, and minerals.**
 
 
 
• **Energy Levels:**
 
 
• **​**Eating three meals a day helps maintain energy levels throughout the day.
 
• This is important as adolescents often** engage in many activities, including school, sports, and hobbies.**
 
 
 
• **Health:**
 
 
• **​**Regular meals contribute to **overall health.**
 
• Skipping meals can lead to** overeating later in the day or choosing fast food and snacks that are not as nutritious.**
 
 
 
• **Habits:**
 
 
• **​**Establishing the habit of having **three meals a day can help adolescents learn about portion sizes and make healthier food choices.**
 
• This habit can also contribute to a balanced diet.
 
 
 
• **Hunger Management:**
 
 
• **​**Eating three meals a day can **help manage hunger levels and prevent overeating or binge eating.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Additional Info about Adolescents:**

 
 
• Adolescence is a transitional stage of **physical and psychological development that generally occurs during the period from puberty to legal adulthood.**
 
• It's a critical period of** growth and development, so proper nutrition is crucial.**
 
• Adolescents require a** higher intake of energy and nutrients compared** to adults because they are growing and developing rapidly.
 
• This includes not only** physical growth but also cognitive development.**
 
• Regular exercise and a **balanced diet can help ensure healthy development during these years.**

questions.question: As per the Census 2011, what was the literacy rate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**74.04%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Literacy Characteristics of India, census 2011:**

 
 
• The results of the 2011 census revealed that there has been an **increase in literacy in the country.**
 
• The literacy rate in the country is **74.04 per cent**
 
• More precisely, **82.14% for males and 65.46% for females.**
 
• **Kerala retained its position by being on top with a 93.91 percent literacy rate.**
 
• The other two States and UTs, followed by Kerala are **Lakshadweep (92.28 percent) and Mizoram (91.58 percent).**
 
• **Bihar with a literacy rate of 63.82 **percent ranks last in the country preceded by Arunachal Pradesh (66.95 percent) and **Rajasthan (67.06 percent).**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Size:**

 
 
• As per the **Census 2011, India's total population was 1.21 billion, making it the world's second-most populous country after China.**
 
• It represented an increase of more than** 181 million people over the population recorded in the 2001 Census.**
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate:**
 
 
• The Census 2011 reported a literacy rate of **74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.**
 
• This marked a significant improvement in** literacy rates compared to the previous census in 2001.**
 
 
 
• **Gender Ratio:**
 
 
• The 2011 Census recorded a gender ratio of **943 females per 1000 males, **which was a slight improvement from the** 2001 Census where the ratio was 933 females per 1000 males.**
 
 
 
• **Urbanization:**
 
• The Census **2011 indicated an increase in urbanization with the urban population accounting for 31.16% of the total population.**
 
• There was a significant rise in the number of towns and cities compared to 2001.
 
• **Largest State:**
 
 
• The most populous state in India, according to the** 2011 Census, was Uttar Pradesh, with over 200 million people.**
 
• The least populous state was **Sikkim, with a population of about 610,000.**

questions.question: Buddha Purnima, celebrated by the devotees of Gautam Buddha, is known as Saga Dawa in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sikkim**

 
 
• **Sikkim **is home to a** significant number of Buddhists and they celebrate Buddha Purnima as Saga Dawa.**
 
• **Saga Dawa** is one of the most important religious events for** Buddhists in Sikkim.**
 
• It marks the** birth, enlightenment, and death (nirvana) of Gautam Buddha.**
 
• It's observed in the fourth month of the Tibetan lunar calendar, which usually falls in May or June.
 
• **The festival involves prayer meetings, processions, and other religious activities in Buddhist monasteries.**
 
• It is a time for increased **almsgiving, meditation, fasting, and other forms of religious devotion among Buddhists.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Who was appointed as the first female Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in August 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__Nallathamby Kalaiselvi__'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Senior scientist Nallathamby Kalaiselvi has become the first woman director general of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), a consortium of 38 research institutes across the country.
 
• She succeeds Shekhar Mande, who superannuated in April. Rajesh Gokhale, Secretary, of the Department of Biotechnology, was given the additional charge of the CSIR upon Mande's retirement.
 
• Known for her work in the field of lithium-ion batteries, Kalaiselvi is at present director of the CSIR-Central Electrochemical Research Institute at Karaikudi in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Kalaiselvi will also hold the charge as secretary, the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research.
 
• Her appointment is for a period of two years with effect from the date of assumption of charge of the post or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
 
• Kalaiselvi also made key contributions to the National Mission for Electric Mobility. She has more than 125 research papers and six patents to her credit.

 [IMAGE: https://st.adda247.com/https://wpassets.adda247.com/wp-content/uploads/multisite/sites/5/2022/08/08090128/67.jpg]
